When I was your age I went to a conference in Germany and met the professor who'd helped my thesis. I bent to touch his feet out of gratitude, and he leapt back like I'd scalded him. "No, no!" he said, and offered a handshake. I turned red. Later, in my grandmother's village, a handshake would have felt cold. So I learned. Now I look at what others do, or ask, "How do you like to greet?" I'm Santosh, and the same gesture can be warmth in one place and intrusion in another.

She hesitated with rain running down her face.

A line on greetings goes into the orientation sheet tomorrow.
